literal: And the completion, and the obstacles, and the resulting benefit that will accrue there upon completion, having examined, one should do.
translation: An action should be undertaken only after carefully considering the effort required for its completion, the obstacles that may arise, and the ultimate benefit that will be gained.
modern: ஒரு செயலை முடிப்பதற்கு ஆகும் முயற்சியையும், இடையில் வரும் இடையூறுகளையும், அது முடிந்த பிறகு கிடைக்கும் பயனையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து அச்செயலைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines three essential factors that must be analyzed before starting any undertaking. First, 'mutivu' refers to the final completion of the task and the resources or effort required to achieve it. Second, 'itaiyuru' represents the potential hindrances or difficulties that might arise along the way. Third, 'patupayan' is the actual profit or utility that will be realized once the task is finished. A wise person weighs all three aspects thoroughly before acting.
